text:
Riley: Heads-up — Skyline Compute reached out to run a joint perf/W + end-to-end throughput validation across their new 'Falcon' boards. They want reproducible artifacts, a short public methodology, and two publishable configs (latency vs efficiency).

Sofia: Nice. Do they want us to ship our runtime container or will they run their optimized binary? Prefer we supply the container so telemetry and instrumentation are consistent.

Skyline CI Bot: Skyline note: partner slots Thu-Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC. We accept partner containers labeled redwood/bench:skyline. Upload prefix s3://redwood-partner-skyline/2045678901/. Per-GPU sensors available + rack PDU.

Marco: For parity I'd like them to run our container. We'll provide a tiny shim to surface their INA sensors as /metrics. Need to agree on measurement windows, warmup behavior, and the model. Suggest "openmix-6B-lite" as canonical.

Riley: Good call. Metrics list: per_gpu_power(W), node_power(W), tokens_per_sec, p95 latency(ms), gpu_util(%), kernel_launch_events, ambient_temp(C). Measurement window: warmup 30s, measure 120s, reps=3.

Legal: Reminder — only aggregated numbers for public release, synthetic-model runs only. No board serials or internal build hashes in any public CSV. We'll need a one-paragraph consent from Skyline legal before publication.

Sofia: Proposed publishable configs: "latency-optimized" (batch=1, seq=256, fp16) and "efficiency-optimized" (batch=4, seq=1024, q5_1). Marketing-friendly names also welcome.

Marco: Kernel tuning knobs I'd like to sweep: launch_coop (on/off), vector_tile (small/large), and prefetch_depth (0/2/4). Also test q5_1 vs fp16 vs int8_equiv. Keep sweep compact (6-8 runs per config). Example sweep file below.

# sweep_table.csv
launch_coop,vector_tile,prefetch_depth,quant,batched
on,small,0,fp16,1
on,large,2,q5_1,4
off,small,4,int8_equiv,1
off,large,0,q5_1,4

Skyline CI Bot: Slot reserved: Thu 02:30 UTC on skyline-ci-falcon-02. Job will post artifacts within +2h after completion.

Riley: Operational asks: (1) Provide a lightweight docker image + README (Riley/Marco). (2) Console dashboard template showing perf/W vs tokens/s and p95 heatmap (Sofia). (3) Legal publish blurb + embargo terms (Legal). (4) Marketing assets request + headline drafts (MKT).

Marco: I'll build the docker image with KV cache disabled by default and a flag REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=enabled for the efficiency runs. Local reproduce command:
```
docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=partner-s3 -v $(pwd)/out:/out redwood/bench:skyline \
  --model openmix-6B-lite --batch $BATCH --seq $SEQ --sweep-file sweep_table.csv \
  --warmup 30 --reps 3 --upload s3://redwood-partner-skyline/2045678901/$RUN_ID
```
Make sure to set SKYLINE_INA_PATH=/sys/skyline/ina if using their sensors.

Sofia: Dashboard widgets: scatter (tokens/s vs perf_per_watt), p95 latency heatmap by config, and an artifacts panel linking to summary.json. Also add an auto-regression eval: tokens/s drop >10% OR perf/W drop >9% to alert #eng-runtime.

MKT: We'll need two headline options and a 48h embargo after legal sign-off. Request Skyline logo and brand kit. Proposed early headlines: "Redwood + Skyline: Efficiency-tuned runtime on Falcon boards" and "Low-latency inference with 2x perf/W on Skyline Falcon" — we'll adapt after numbers.

Legal: I'll send a short publication consent template to Skyline legal requesting permission to publish aggregated CSVs and the co-authored methodology. Also ask for explicit permission if they want per-GPU numbers quoted.

OpsBot: CI will upload artifacts at $UPLOAD_PATH/logs.tar.gz and $UPLOAD_PATH/summary.json. Publishable CSV path will be $UPLOAD_PATH/publishable.csv (node-averaged).

Marco: Small note on timing: for efficiency runs, enable KV cache; for latency runs, disable it. Document that in methodology. Also annotate whether power is from per-GPU sensor or PDU.

Skyline CI Bot: Run completed: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-partner-skyline/2045678901/logs.tar.gz (link: https://s3.example/2045678901/logs.tar.gz). Summary at s3://redwood-partner-skyline/2045678901/summary.json.

Riley: Thanks — please post the aggregated CSV (node averages, no serials) and a short numbers summary here. We'll then route to Legal for publish review.

Marco: Parsed summary and uploaded publishable CSV to s3://redwood-partner-skyline/2045678901/publishable.csv. Quick preview: efficiency (q5_1) shows ~2.3x perf/W vs fp16 baseline at a 9% p95 increase; latency config (fp16, batch=1) stayed within 3% of baseline latency with a 1.6x throughput improvement.

Legal: Received — I'll circulate the publishable blurb to Skyline legal and confirm embargo window (requesting 72h). If Skyline approves, we'll schedule a short co-author review.

MKT: Great. Once legal confirms, we'll draft the blog and prepare the marketplace badge copy.

Sofia: Closing notes: remember to tag any public material with both companies and include the methodology appendix (warmup exclusion, measurement window, sensor source). If no objections, I'll close the thread after legal sign-off. :+1:

Riley: No objections. Thanks everyone.
